patients.label: Case 3: 49-year-old woman with DRPLA, dementia, epilepsy and corneal endothelial degeneration without optic atrophy

identity_evidence.quote: A 49-year-old woman developed gait ataxia and intellectual disability in her 30s

attribution_limitations: Visual acuity of 20/200 in both eyes is stated by the authors to be unreliable because of dementia.
Symptom onset wording differs between text (gait ataxia in her 30s; seizures at 35 years old) and Table 1 ("Ataxia and epilepsy at 35 y/o"); not a numeric conflict.
Table 1 remarks "A wheelchair needed" has no counterpart in the case text; Table 1 also records dystonia and dementia with epilepsy.

patients.label: Case 4: 51-year-old woman with DRPLA and corneal endothelial degeneration (bullous keratopathy) treated with corneal transplantation

identity_evidence.quote: A 51-year-old woman has no observed abnormalities

attribution_limitations: The text says laser in situ keratomileusis was part of the past ocular history "when she noticed a visual disturbance at 49 years old"; the surgery date and eye are not stated.

Descemet's stripping endothelial keratoplasty and the later 'corneal transplantation in the left eye' may be the same operation, but the source does not identify them as one event; the Discussion also places cataract surgery before the transplantation.
Table 1 records optic atrophy as negative while the text reports inferior RNFL thinning on OCT that the authors call unreliable because of a tilted disk from high myopia.

Source conflict between the main text (specular microscopy showed no corneal guttata or rounded dark cells) and the Supplementary Figure 3 caption (SM3: rounded dark cells with light borders on panel A, the right eye).
Corneal transplantation laterality is the left eye; the laterality of the earlier Descemet stripping and of bullous keratopathy is not stated.

caption_claims.text:
Figure 1
Pedigree of the family with dentatorubral-pallidoluysian atrophy (DRPLA), including the four patients in this study. Pedigree of the family with DRPLA showing generations (Roman numerals) of affected (solid symbols) and unaffected (open symbols) members. Roman numerals represent generation numbers. Squares indicate male members; circles, female members; P, proband; oblique, deceased; optic A, optic atrophy; corneal D, corneal endothelial degeneration. Genetic analysis (E+) shows the expanded allele of CAG repeats at the DRPLA locus (III-5, III-10, IV-1, and IV-3).

evidence.quote: Pedigree of the family with dentatorubral-pallidoluysian atrophy (DRPLA), including the four patients in this study.

caption_claims.text:
Figure 2
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings in the present four patients. (A) Patient 1 (III-10). Fluid attenuated inversion recovery images of the MRI show diffuse cerebellar and brainstem atrophy, as well as high-intensity signals in the diffuse periventricular white matter. (B) Patient 2 (III-5). MRI shows diffuse cerebellar and brainstem atrophy, as well as high-intensity signals in the diffuse periventricular white matter. (C) Patient 3 (IV-3). MRI shows diffuse cerebellar and brainstem atrophy without white matter changes. (D) Patient 4 (IV-1). MRI shows diffuse cerebellar atrophy without periventricular white matter changes.

evidence.quote: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings in the present four patients.

caption_claims.text:
Figure 3
Endothelial corneal cell density (ECD) and circumpapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) in Patient 1 (III-10). Specular microscopy (FA-3609, Konan Medical, Inc. Japan) shows (B) corneal guttata, (A,B) pleomorphic cellular patterns of endothelial structures, and (B) rounded dark cells with light borders. The corneal cell density is 483 and 444 cells/mm^(2) in the (A) right and (B) left eyes, respectively. (C–E) An optical coherence tomography (OCT: 3D CT-2000, Topcon Medical Japan, Co. Ltd, Japan) indicates the ocular fundus color photograph, RNFL thickness map, super Pixel-200 image, and RNFL values in the circular areas. An OCT shows RNFL thinning in the superior (55 μm) and inferior (57 μm) areas of the (C) right eye and inferior area (84 μm) of the (E) left eye.

caption_claims.text:
Figure 1
Pedigree of the family with dentatorubral-pallidoluysian atrophy (DRPLA), including the four patients in this study. Pedigree of the family with DRPLA showing generations (Roman numerals) of affected (solid symbols) and unaffected (open symbols) members. Roman numerals represent generation numbers. Squares indicate male members; circles, female members; P, proband; oblique, deceased; optic A, optic atrophy; corneal D, corneal endothelial degeneration. Genetic analysis (E+) shows the expanded allele of CAG repeats at the DRPLA locus (III-5, III-10, IV-1, and IV-3).

Figure 2
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings in the present four patients. (A) Patient 1 (III-10). Fluid attenuated inversion recovery images of the MRI show diffuse cerebellar and brainstem atrophy, as well as high-intensity signals in the diffuse periventricular white matter. (B) Patient 2 (III-5). MRI shows diffuse cerebellar and brainstem atrophy, as well as high-intensity signals in the diffuse periventricular white matter. (C) Patient 3 (IV-3). MRI shows diffuse cerebellar and brainstem atrophy without white matter changes. (D) Patient 4 (IV-1). MRI shows diffuse cerebellar atrophy without periventricular white matter changes.

Figure 1
Pedigree of the family with dentatorubral-pallidoluysian atrophy (DRPLA), including the four patients in this study. Pedigree of the family with DRPLA showing generations (Roman numerals) of affected (solid symbols) and unaffected (open symbols) members. Roman numerals represent generation numbers. caption_claims.text:
Figure 1
Pedigree of the family with dentatorubral-pallidoluysian atrophy (DRPLA), including the four patients in this study. Pedigree of the family with DRPLA showing generations (Roman numerals) of affected (solid symbols) and unaffected (open symbols) members. Roman numerals represent generation numbers. Squares indicate male members; circles, female members; P, proband; oblique, deceased; optic A, optic atrophy; corneal D, corneal endothelial degeneration. Genetic analysis (E+) shows the expanded allele of CAG repeats at the DRPLA locus (III-5, III-10, IV-1, and IV-3).

evidence.quote: Pedigree of the family with dentatorubral-pallidoluysian atrophy (DRPLA), including the four patients in this study.

caption_claims.text:
Figure 2
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings in the present four patients. (A) Patient 1 (III-10). Fluid attenuated inversion recovery images of the MRI show diffuse cerebellar and brainstem atrophy, as well as high-intensity signals in the diffuse periventricular white matter. (B) Patient 2 (III-5). MRI shows diffuse cerebellar and brainstem atrophy, as well as high-intensity signals in the diffuse periventricular white matter. (C) Patient 3 (IV-3). MRI shows diffuse cerebellar and brainstem atrophy without white matter changes. (D) Patient 4 (IV-1). MRI shows diffuse cerebellar atrophy without periventricular white matter changes.
